title: Journey mapping and sprint templates for version turnover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: create a repeatable, cross-functional playbook that maps the customer journey and the internal sprint cadence required to retire older model versions or change major API behavior with minimal disruption. This ticket produces: 1) a matrix that ties code-level blockers/deps to customer-facing milestones, 2) sprint templates for PM/Eng/Design/Support to run migration sprints, and 3) a canonical release-notes and comms bundle that can be reused across product lines. We will prioritize clarity for self-serve customers while also defining a concierge path for high-touch enterprise accounts.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical customer-journey matrix (CSV) that lists customer states, expected actions, and recommended comms at T-90/T-60/T-30/T-14/T-7/T-0/post-30d
Sprint templates for PM/Eng/Design/Support sized for 2-week cycles (playbook doc + checklist)
A release-notes template with sections for impact, mitigation, migration steps, sample code, and rollback guidance
Comms calendar (email, in-product banner, changelog, account manager outreach) validated with Growth and Sales Ops
Automated link to a customer-facing migration advisor (spec in doc) that surfaces equivalence mapping for deprecated flags/params
At least one dry-run runbook used in a single-team pilot (postmortem recorded)
tasks: Draft customer-journey matrix and initial mapping to code dependencies (owner: PM)
Work with Eng to identify blocking migrations and required SDK/API changes (owner: Eng lead)
Design in-product messaging wireframes for banner and modal flows (owner: Design)
Create release-notes template and sample filled example for a past deprecation to validate tone and signal strength (owner: PM)
Coordinate with Support to create canned responses and triage rubric (owner: Support lead)
Book 30-min alignment workshop with Sales/Account Management to define concierge eligibility and escalation SLA (owner: PM)
Wire up confluence page and link to GitHub PRs, dashboard alerts, and runbook (owner: PM)
Run a pilot with a low-risk feature to validate sprint template and comm cadence; capture metrics (owner: PM + Eng)
Iterate on the playbook based on pilot feedback and finalize for org-wide use (owner: PM)
Publish playbook and announce in All Hands + internal Slack channel #product-ops (owner: PM)
Add a job to console release checklist to attach playbook when any API/contract change is detected (owner: Release Manager)

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Enterprise customers may require bespoke migration plans -> Mitigation: early account outreach and concierge lane; include AM in alignment workshop.
Risk: Insufficient telemetry to target high-risk customers -> Mitigation: ENG-30211 addresses missing signal; move to top of dependencies.
Risk: Overloading Support at T-7/T-0 -> Mitigation: progressive disclosure + staggered notices and dedicated triage rotations during launch window.
Risk: Confusing release notes language causing false-positives in automated SDKs -> Mitigation: include code snippets and equivalence table; run static analyzer on sample clients.
comm_cadence: T-90: Public release note (changelog) announcing intent and high-level timeline
T-60: Detailed migration guide published; account managers notified of customers above threshold
T-30: In-product banner enabled for users seen in telemetry; community forum post with Q&A
T-14: Targeted emails to affected customers with migration steps and sample code
T-7: Escalation window opens; concierge onboarding available for eligible accounts
T-0: Change executed; in-product notice updated to reflect completion; monitoring and rollback hooks on-call
Post+30d: Follow-up summary and customer impact report published internally
pilot_notes: Pilot candidate: Storage indexing API flag removal (low-risk), planned dry-run in Cycle 12
Pilot success metrics: <10% unexpected support tickets, <2% usage regression in critical paths, migration docs completion rate >75% among sampled customers
Pilot timeline: prep week, communication week, execution week, and 2-week observation window
postmortem_template: Customer impact and notable accounts affected
